edge_cases: Missing or malformed JSON fields cause a server error (400/500).
Non‑numeric poll_id or option_id values may break the SQL query.
Empty options list when creating a poll results in no option rows.
Repeated votes from the same voter_id are not prevented.
Very long title or option strings may exceed database column limits.
SQL injection payloads can alter the database because queries are not parameterized.
contract.intent: Expose a web API for creating polls, recording votes, and fetching poll results.
invariants: Each poll must have a unique integer poll_id generated by the database.
Option rows reference an existing poll_id.
Vote rows reference existing poll_id and option_id values.
The JSON response structure and HTTP status codes remain consistent.
io_behavior: POST /create_poll with JSON {title, options} returns 201 and JSON {message, poll_id}.
POST /vote with JSON {poll_id, option_id, voter_id} returns 200 and JSON {message}.
GET /get_results?poll_id=ID returns 200 and JSON array of {option_text, vote_count} objects.
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the polls table.
Inserts one row per option into the options table linked to the poll.
Inserts a new row into the votes table for each vote recorded.
Commits the above changes to the SQLite database file.

rationale: Core API endpoints, responses, and database writes match the contract, but the implementation adds validation that prevents several listed edge‑case failures (empty options, non‑numeric IDs, SQL injection), altering the original error‑behaviour.
